shortDescription: Ireland's services sector expanded at a strong pace for the fifth straight month in October as activity and new business again rose, though inflation concerns darkened the outlook, a business survey showed on Wednesday.

children: Ireland's services sector expanded at a strong pace for the fifth straight month in October as activity and new business again rose, though inflation concerns darkened the outlook, a business survey showed on Wednesday.
The AIB Ireland Services Business Activity Index, compiled by S&P Global, rose to 54.3 in October from 54.1 in September
That was well above the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction. It has only slipped below that level once in more than five years, in April of this year

New business also grew for a sixth month, but the pace eased from September. International demand was weaker, with new export business stalling as gains in technology, media and telecoms, and tourism-related services were offset by declines elsewhere
Employment increased for a second successive month, though the pace remained modest and below the long-run survey average
Cost pressures intensified, with input price inflation climbing to a five-month high and its third-strongest rate since February 2023, driven by fuel, energy, wages and supply shortages
Prices charged rose at the sharpest pace since February 2023 to a near four-year high as firms passed costs on to their customers
Companies' outlooks for the next 12 months weakened sharply as a result, with the future activity index falling to a six-month low and recording its biggest month-on-month drop since March 2022
A number of survey respondents mentioned that high inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty were undermining the outlook, AIB Chief Economist David McNamara said

title: Irish services growth stays strong but inflation concerns hit outlook, PMI shows
